controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by Kepler-11; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured color.
controls.notes: No image or color of Kepler-11 e is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the color of kepler-11's light, as its color dataset measures it.

charts.alt: The orbits of Kepler-11's planets in this map from above, to scale, with Kepler-11 e highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

Kepler-11 e crossing its star, as Kepler recorded it: 17 quarters (1 to 17) of the Kepler pipeline's 30-minute light curves of KIC 6541920, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, moved 8 minutes later to where Kepler measures the dip, inside the published ephemeris's 3-sigma uncertainty of 9 minutes at these dates, then averaged in 30-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.

physical.credit: Radius from Lissauer et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...770..131L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; mass from Lissauer et al. 2013, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2013ApJ...770..131L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; orbit from Lissauer et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...770..131L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive
